title: BenchX measurement result ingest object
description: One measurement attempt for one quantity and one workload variant, as reported by a producer. See docs/design/benchmark-result-schema.md section 5. Producers report coordinates and evidence; comparison identity, series, and series points are derived by the server and are never part of this message.
$comment: Rules the schema cannot express and the server enforces at ingest: the primary subject component's source, when present, equals the top-level source URI; a quantity's unit never changes once used in a project; at most one estimate summary per estimator declaration; results sharing an attempt_key agree on the fields listed in section 5.3; identical (producer, ingest_key) payloads are idempotent and differing ones conflict; UCUM unit syntax; interval lower bounds not exceeding upper bounds; completed_repetitions never exceeding attempted_repetitions, and likewise completed never exceeding attempted at each repetition level; exactly one provenance.references entry per compound input role; comparison profiles (section 5.5) are checked by the comparator, not here. A result without project or benchmark is thin (section 4.1): valid, comparable within its run, and joinable to tracked series only through an approved mapping.

schema_version.description: Message contract version this object conforms to.

producer.description: Stable, namespaced identity of the adapter or harness that produced this message, plus its software and mapping versions. Only the name is part of the idempotency key.

mapping_version.description: Version of the native-to-BenchX mapping applied by the producer.

ingest_key.description: Producer-scoped idempotency key. Unique per result under one producer name; must distinguish workload variant, quantity, and attempt.

attempt_key.description: Globally namespace-qualified key, such as a URI-like key or UUID, shared by every result from one concrete execution of one workload variant. A retry gets a new key.

project.description: Namespace for project-defined names and policy. Optional only for thin local results.

source.description: Designated subject source whose revisions form the history axis.

revision.description: Subject revision measured, keyed by the clean VCS identifier. Dirty state is a provenance flag.

benchmark.description: Exact code that defined and executed the workload. A reported coordinate that policy normally maps to a declared benchmark version. Optional only for thin local results with no benchmark repository. The revision may be omitted when the benchmark code has no version control; provenance.benchmark_tree then identifies it and benchmark_dirty is dirty.

coordinates.description: Reported coordinates: what was measured and under which conditions. Fingerprinted as reported; identity policy projects them into comparison identity.

workload.description: Workload variant: a named operation plus one resolved parameter assignment.

parameters.description: One concrete parameter assignment. Values are primitives or arrays of primitives. A baseline-versus-variant study uses a `role` parameter.

dataset.description: Identity of the input data. Part of the workload variant, so runs on different data never share a variant.

parameters.description: Generation parameters such as row count or seed.

subject.description: Implementation or system under test. Exactly one component has role 'primary' and is the designated source; other components are pinned coordinates.

configuration.description: How the artifact under test was built or configured: build type, compiler, flags, JIT/AOT mode, backend.

quantity.description: Measured quantity and its canonical UCUM unit. Distinct measurement semantics require distinct names.

comparison_context.description: How the subject is exercised and measured: intended settings such as protocol version, host runtime, warmup and calibration policy, timer.

environment.description: Host or allocation shared by every result of the attempt.

schema.description: Identity schema that defines which identity fields exist and how they are hashed.

identity.description: Fields that define environment identity under the named schema.

metadata.description: Descriptive facts that do not enter environment identity.

resource_selection.description: Optional resource this result applies to within the environment: CPU/core set, GPU UUID or device index, accelerator partition.

measurement.description: Outcome and producer evidence for this quantity.

reason.description: Machine-readable lowercase token such as 'timeout' or 'resource-exhausted.memory'. Required for every status except success.

observations.description: Observation batch: finite values in the quantity's canonical unit after declared normalization. Numbers, or structured observations carrying per-observation metadata.

derivation.description: For a compound result with a pairwise batch: the per-pair rule that produced the observations, declared as a compound estimator at input_level observations (section 4.5).

summaries.description: Typed producer summaries. Server-derived values never appear here.

observed_context.description: Immutable per-result snapshot of conditions allowed to vary within a series, such as kernel, glibc, microcode, load, temperature. Never enters identity.

procedure.description: Realized batch-wide acquisition details. Per-observation metadata belongs on structured observations instead.

repetition_levels.description: Realized counterpart of a multi-level protocol.repetitions, outermost level first. Counts are totals over the attempt, so 20 processes of 3 values each attempt 20 processes and 60 values. attempted_repetitions and completed_repetitions remain the totals at the innermost level.

caches_cleared.description: Caches actually dropped during the attempt, in order.

slot.description: Position of this attempt in the run's realized order across all sides, zero-based. The intended schedule is comparison_context.protocol.schedule.

timeout_seconds.description: Limit the run author imposed on the attempt, recorded whether or not it fired. An attempt stopped by it is error with reason timeout, not censored.

round.description: Position of this attempt in an interleaved run, monotone per run and kept by a retry. Attempts with the same round number across sides of a comparison are paired.

provenance.description: Audit metadata. Nothing here enters comparison identity.
provenance.$comment: A tree id is required whenever the matching dirty flag is clean or dirty, and absent when it is unknown.

run_key.description: Grouping key assigned by the run author: scheduler, CLI, or CI system.

labels.description: Caller-supplied labels for selecting sides of a comparison, such as {"env": "numpy-2.0"}. Never enter identity.

native_id.description: Identifier of this result in the producer's native system.

started_at.description: Measurement start on the producer's clock. The only fact that orders attempts across runs; ingest time is never used.

subject_tree.description: Content hash of the measured subject checkout: the git tree object id of the working tree, or a native equivalent. Equal ids mean identical code regardless of commit.

benchmark_dirty.description: unknown when no benchmark repository exists or its state could not be determined.

benchmark_tree.description: Content hash of the measured benchmark checkout, as for subject_tree.

runner.description: Audit-only identity of the runner software.

original_unit.description: Unit used by the producer before normalization to the canonical unit.

references.description: Stable references to other results in the same run: compound-estimator inputs by role, or an anchor measurement. Never enter identity.

artifacts.description: External evidence such as large observation sets, profiles, or histograms.

info.description: Open descriptive metadata: logs, notes, corrections.

quality.description: Immutable producer-side validation and warnings. Store-side quarantine and exclusion are separate state.

validation.description: Producer-observed validation facts. The verdict that acts on them is decision policy.

correctness.description: Outcome of a harness-run correctness check against expected output.

allOf.$comment: A compound declaration, in an estimate summary or in measurement.derivation, needs provenance.references so each input role resolves to a stored result.
A benchmark without a revision is identified by its tree alone, and an unversioned tree cannot be shown to be clean.

treeId.description: Lowercase hex content hash of a working tree: 40 characters for git SHA-1 repositories, 64 for SHA-256 ones or other hash schemes.

dirtyState.description: Working-tree state of the measured checkout. unknown is distinct from clean so comparators can reject anything not known to be clean.

timestamp.$comment: format is an annotation in draft 2020-12; the pattern is the assertion.

type.description: Source kind, such as git, hg, or dataset.

key.description: Clean VCS identifier or other native revision key.

native_order.description: Optional order metadata from the native system when the source cannot supply topology.

resultRef.description: Stable reference to a stored result.

then.$comment: The primary component's revision is the top-level revision; its source, if given, must equal the top-level source URI.

estimator.description: Estimator declaration. Name, method version, parameters, input level, and input roles enter the estimator fingerprint.

parameters.description: Details that can alter the value, such as percentile interpolation.

inputs.description: Semantic input roles of a compound estimator.

slot.description: Position of this observation in the run's realized order across all sides, for observation-level interleaving.

constraint.description: Quantitative constraint for censored results: kind, finite bound(s), inclusivity of each bound present, and cause. Fields present must match the kind.

summarySource.description: Every summary in an ingest object is producer evidence.

intervalSummary.description: Confidence or coverage interval for a named statistic at a stated level.

sourceBoundsSummary.description: Opaque bounds whose exact semantics are unknown. The label preserves source terminology such as stat, sys, range, or error.
